From 3027e7b15b02d2d37e3f82d6b8404f6d37e3b8cf Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Kunwu Chan <chentao@kylinos.cn>
Date: Tue, 12 Dec 2023 10:40:15 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] ice: Fix some null pointer dereference issues in ice_ptp.c

devm_kasprintf() returns a pointer to dynamically allocated memory
which can be NULL upon failure.

Fixes: d938a8cca88a ("ice: Auxbus devices & driver for E822 TS")
Cc: Kunwu Chan <kunwu.chan@hotmail.com>
Suggested-by: Przemek Kitszel <przemyslaw.kitszel@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Kunwu Chan <chentao@kylinos.cn>
Reviewed-by: Przemek Kitszel <przemyslaw.kitszel@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Simon Horman <horms@kernel.org>
Tested-by: Pucha Himasekhar Reddy <himasekharx.reddy.pucha@intel.com> (A Contingent worker at Intel)
Signed-off-by: Tony Nguyen <anthony.l.nguyen@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_ptp.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_ptp.c
index c4fe28017b8d..3b6605c8585e 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_ptp.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/intel/ice/ice_ptp.c
@@ -2863,6 +2863,8 @@ static int ice_ptp_register_auxbus_driver(struct ice_pf *pf)
 	name = devm_kasprintf(dev, GFP_KERNEL, "ptp_aux_dev_%u_%u_clk%u",
 			      pf->pdev->bus->number, PCI_SLOT(pf->pdev->devfn),
 			      ice_get_ptp_src_clock_index(&pf->hw));
+	if (!name)
+		return -ENOMEM;
 
 	aux_driver->name = name;
 	aux_driver->shutdown = ice_ptp_auxbus_shutdown;
@@ -3109,6 +3111,8 @@ static int ice_ptp_create_auxbus_device(struct ice_pf *pf)
 	name = devm_kasprintf(dev, GFP_KERNEL, "ptp_aux_dev_%u_%u_clk%u",
 			      pf->pdev->bus->number, PCI_SLOT(pf->pdev->devfn),
 			      ice_get_ptp_src_clock_index(&pf->hw));
+	if (!name)
+		return -ENOMEM;
 
 	aux_dev->name = name;
 	aux_dev->id = id;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `ice_ptp.c`**
1. **Line Addition (2863)**: After the call to `devm_kasprintf`, a check is added to verify if `name` is NULL. If it is, the function returns `-ENOMEM`, indicating memory allocation failure.
2. **Line Addition (3109)**: Similarly, another check is added after a second call to `devm_kasprintf` to ensure that `name` is not NULL. If it is NULL, the function also returns `-ENOMEM`.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modifications in `ice_ptp.c` are related in that they both address potential null pointer dereference issues caused by the `devm_kasprintf` function, which can return NULL if memory allocation fails. By adding checks for NULL after each allocation, the code now properly handles memory allocation failures, preventing crashes or undefined behavior in the driver. This change enhances the robustness of the driver by ensuring that it gracefully handles errors related to memory allocation.

You are a programming expert.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
name = devm_kasprintf(dev, GFP_KERNEL, "ptp_aux_dev_%u_%u_clk%u",
                      pf->pdev->bus->number, PCI_SLOT(pf->pdev->devfn),
                      ice_get_ptp_src_clock_index(&pf->hw));
```
```c
aux_driver->name = name;
```
```c
aux_dev->name = name;
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because the code does not check if `devm_kasprintf` returns NULL, which can happen if memory allocation fails. If `name` is NULL, the subsequent assignments to `aux_driver->name` and `aux_dev->name` will lead to null pointer dereference issues when the code attempts to use these pointers.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (!name)
    return -ENOMEM;
```
Reason:
This check ensures that if `devm_kasprintf` returns NULL, the function will return an error code (-ENOMEM) immediately, preventing any further dereferencing of the NULL pointer and thus avoiding the null pointer dereference issues.
